subject: mathematics
question_text: Define a symmetric matrix. If the matrix with rows (−1, 2, 3), (2, 5, 6) and (3, x, 7) is symmetric, find the value of x.

recall_prompt: Say what a symmetric matrix is and how you would find x.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Define symmetric
steps.margin_note: First mark. The question says "define", so write the definition: A is symmetric when A equals its own transpose.
lines: A square matrix A is symmetric if A = Aᵀ.

recall.must_convey: That a square matrix is symmetric when it equals its own transpose, A = Aᵀ.
accept: a square matrix is symmetric if it equals its transpose
symmetric means A equals A transpose
the matrix is the same as its transpose
symmetric ante A equals A transpose
A is symmetric when transposing changes nothing

steps.why: "Define" is worth a mark by itself. The number alone answers half the question.
common_mistakes: Defining it as A = −Aᵀ, which is skew symmetric.

steps.label: Equate the mirror entries
steps.margin_note: Second mark. In a symmetric matrix the entry in row 3 column 2 equals the entry in row 2 column 3. Those are x and 6.
lines: A = Aᵀ, so the (3,2) entry equals the (2,3) entry:

recall.must_convey: That symmetry makes the (3,2) entry equal the (2,3) entry, so x = 6.
accept: symmetry means the entry in row three column two equals the one in row two column three so x is six
the mirror entry across the diagonal is six so x equals six
equating the reflected positions gives x is six
diagonal ki reflect ayina entry six kabatti x equals six
x must match the six on the other side of the diagonal

steps.why: Symmetry is a reflection across the principal diagonal, so every entry is tied to the one in the mirrored position. Only one pair here contains an unknown.
common_mistakes: Matching x with the 3 in the first row.
Equating x with a diagonal entry.
